concur

/kən-KUR/ — rhymes with her · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To concur with someone is to agree with their opinion, decision, or judgment.

All three doctors concurred that surgery was unnecessary.

Example

After studying the research data, even the skeptical board member had to concur with the majority's conclusion about the trend.

Concur is more precise than 'agree' here because it emphasizes that the skeptical member reached a shared judgment after deliberation, not just casual assent.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

assent: To assent is to formally say yes to something placed before you — a plan, a request, a proposal that someone else drew up. To concur is different: no one hands you anything to approve. Experts concur when each examines the evidence and independently reaches the same judgment.

align: To align is to bring your position into agreement with someone else's — you adjust your stance to match theirs, often for unity or strategy. To concur requires no adjusting at all: your own independent judgment simply lands in the same place as another's. Allies align; independent experts concur.

concede: To concede is to admit a point reluctantly, after resisting it — you give ground because you can no longer defend your side. To concur carries no reluctance and no defeat: experts concur when their own judgment genuinely matches, not because they lost the argument.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dissent: to disagree openly with an opinion

differ: to hold a different opinion from someone

Where it sits · how fully you stand behind the opinion — comply → agree → concur → endorse

comply vs. concur: Comply is the weakest: you can comply with a decision you privately dislike, but to concur is to genuinely share the opinion behind it.

agree vs. concur: Agree is the everyday, general word for sharing the same opinion, while concur is a notch stronger and more formal — experts concur when, after careful judgment, their conclusions match exactly.

endorse vs. concur: Endorse goes beyond concur: to concur is to share an opinion, but to endorse is to publicly stamp your approval on it and urge others to accept it too.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con- (com-)

Prefix — con- (com-): together (Latin)

Root — cur(r)

Root — cur(r): to run (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- ('together') + cur ('to run') paints a picture of ideas running together along the same path — when you concur, your opinion runs right alongside someone else's.

Use the root in a new word: current

Use the root in a new word: current: The river's current runs swiftly toward the sea — current comes from the same Latin root currere, 'to run,' that lets concur describe opinions running together.

Word Choice

formal

Concur is more formal and precise than 'agree.' Use it when describing an important judgment or decision reached after deliberation, especially in professional or academic settings. For casual agreement, 'agree' is simpler and more natural.
